chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿUmar ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a muḥṣanah woman who committed zina while she was pregnant. He said: “She is left until she delivers what is in her womb and nurses her child, then she is stoned.”

She committed illicit intercourse. She said: “I was in an open land, and intense thirst struck me. Then a tent appeared to me, so I came to it and found in it a Bedouin man. I asked him for water, but he refused to give me water unless I yielded myself to him. So I turned away from him fleeing. Then the thirst became severe upon me until my eyes sank and my tongue failed. When it reached that point with me, I went to him, and he gave me water and had intercourse with me.”

So he عليه السلام said to him: “This is the one about whom Allah, Exalted is He, said: ‘But whoever is compelled, neither seeking nor transgressing’—this one was neither seeking nor transgressing toward him.” So he let her go.
Then ʿUmar said: “Were it not for ʿAlī, ʿUmar would have perished.”

key_terms.بَاغٍ: one seeking wrongdoing or acting willfully in transgression
key_terms.تُرْجَمُ: she is stoned, referring to the legal punishment of rajm
key_terms.تُرْضِعَ: she nurses or suckles her child
key_terms.زَنَتْ: committed zina, meaning illicit sexual intercourse
key_terms.عَادٍ: one exceeding lawful bounds or transgressing
key_terms.مُحْصَنَةٍ: a previously married or legally protected woman subject to the ḥadd of rajm in the context of zina

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a pregnant woman convicted of zina, and is a woman excused if extreme thirst forced her into it?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses two legal situations related to zina: the delayed punishment of a pregnant muḥṣanah woman until after childbirth and nursing, and the exemption of a woman coerced by extreme necessity. It also applies the Qur’anic principle of compulsion to show that one who is forced by dire need is not treated as willingly transgressing.
